title: Banner landmark should not be nested
summary: A banner landmark sits inside another landmark such as main. Move the site header to the top level of the page.
problem: An element with role="banner" is placed inside another landmark, here <main>. The banner is meant to be the site-wide header, so it should be a direct part of the page, not a piece of the content area.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users list landmarks to understand a page. A banner nested inside main muddles that list and makes the structure harder to trust, so it is harder to tell where the site header ends and the content begins.
steps: Find the element with role="banner", or the page-level <header>, that sits inside main, aside, nav or another landmark.
Move it out so it is a direct child of <body>, before <main>.
If the element is only a heading area for one section of the content, remove role="banner" and use a plain <header> inside a <section> or <article>, which is not a banner.
Keep only one banner per page.
before:
Fernwood Garden Supply

Spring sale

Raised beds, compost and tools.

12 Mill Lane
after:
Fernwood Garden Supply

Spring sale

Raised beds, compost and tools.

12 Mill Lane
whyItMatters: This is a recommended practice rather than a WCAG failure. A banner at the top level gives assistive technology a reliable landmark for the site header, which the same way every page of your site should use.
howToCheck: Open the browser accessibility tree or a landmarks extension and check that the banner is not shown indented under main or another landmark.
